newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips profit slumps, big extraordinary charge due.
newsitem.headline: Philips profit slumps, big extraordinary charge due.

text.p: Dutch electronics giant Philips Electronics NV Thursday reported a slump in third-quarter profit and warned of a one billion guilder ($584 million) extraordinary charge in the current final quarter.
In early Amsterdam trading, Philips shares plunged 3.20 guilders or more than five percent to 53.40 after the news, which was worse than market analysts had expected.
But the stock later recovered to 55.60 guilders, down 1.00 guilder on the day.

Third-quarter net profit from normal operations fell to 123 million guilders ($71.9 million) from 539 million ($315 million) a year ago. Analysts had expected earnings of between 240 and 360 million guilders ($140 million and $211 million).

Some analysts had expected Philips to make a third-quarter charge to cover continuing restructuring but new president Cor Boonstra instead gave advance warning of a one billion guilder ($584 million) extraordinary charge in the fourth quarter.

"Analysis of our business...demonstrates the need to accelerate planned actions for recovery. Consequently we anticipate we will recognise a charge in the fourth quarter of 1996 of approximately one billion guilders before tax," he said.
Boonstra told reporters in Eindhoven that the third-quarter business performance was "very, very disappointing."
"The anticipated recovery of sales and income has not materialised," the group said in a statement.
Philips said income from normal operations more than halved in the first nine months of 1996 to 804 million guilders ($470 million) or 2.35 guilders per share.

"In addition to the lower than expected sales growth and increasing price erosion in various markets, income was affected by unfavourable developments particularly in the semiconductor industry and in passive components, and the costs associated with our entry into the consumer communications business," it said.
Comparable sales growth for the group in the nine months was 6 percent versus 12 percent a year earlier. Price erosion was 4 percent compared with two percent in the same 1995 period.
Analysts said they were disappointed with the poor third-quarter numbers.

"Very disappointing," said Joost van Beek at Van Meer James Capel. "When you look at the breakdown it is particularly disappointing in the lighting and semi-conductor areas. I was already quite pessimistic but this surpasses that."
